title: Justified text hyphenates words to even out its spacing
body:
`text-align justify` (acre-2457be) breaks a paragraph only at spaces, and `text::even_breaks` in `crates/acre/src/text.rs` chooses among those breaks. Spaces never shrink, so in a narrow `width` some lines come out loose. A trial at 180 pixels with 14-pixel text set "suffix   of   a   text   in" with spaces several times their width, because the next word did not fit.

TeX hyphenates words for this reason. Each place a word may break adds one more choice of where a line ends, and with more choices the breaker finds lines that fill the width with spaces close to their natural size. Knuth and Plass count a break at a hyphen as a candidate with a penalty, `\hyphenpenalty` 50 in plain TeX, so the breaker hyphenates only when it buys evener spacing.

## Proposal

Let `even_breaks` also break inside a word, at the points Liang's hyphenation patterns allow, with a penalty, and end such a line with a hyphen glyph.

## Cost

- Patterns per language. English patterns are tens of kilobytes. A crate such as `hyphenation` embeds them, which adds a dependency and its licence terms to the library.
- Shaping. Words are shaped whole by rustybuzz, and a break point inside a ligature such as "ffi" has no glyph boundary. The word would have to be shaped again as two pieces, with a hyphen shaped in the first one's font.
- Text. The PDF writer copies `Layout::text` out by glyph. A hyphen the layout added is not in that text, so copying would need to leave it out or map it.
- Code spans and formulas never hyphenate, and neither should names in mono.
- Ragged text would stay as it is, so existing figures do not move.
